finding.claim: Negative amount on /transfer lets any authenticated account holder drain any other existing account. The balance guard at line 11 is false for any negative value, so the sender is credited and the victim debited by |amount| with no upper bound.
finding.source: JSON body field 'amount' (line 10), attacker-controlled; requires an authenticated session whose identity is set outside this file (see AUTH-1).

trace.note: amount read from request.json without sign validation
guard BAL[g.user] < amount is False for negative amount, so no abort
sender balance increases by |amount|
victim balance decreases by |amount|

finding.guards_checked: /withdraw rejects amount <= 0 (line 21) but /transfer has no equivalent check; no other validation on the path. Severity HIGH: triage Check 13 requires confirmed external reachability and an unauthenticated path, which this file cannot establish.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. bank.py:11 is the only check on /transfer: BAL[g.user] < amount is False for any negative amount, so abort(400) never fires. No sign check on amount (bank.py:10), no before_request hook, and no other .py file exists in the directory. The /withdraw check at bank.py:21 is not on the /transfer path.
verdict.reason: bank.py:10 takes amount unvalidated, bank.py:11 lets any negative amount through, and bank.py:13-14 credit g.user and debit `to` by |amount| with no upper bound. The attacker needs only a valid session, since g.user comes from outside this file, so this is confirmed as a logic flaw; the HIGH severity rating depends on the auth path (AUTH-1), which this file cannot establish.

finding.claim: JSON NaN as amount bypasses all balance checks. Python json (used by Flask request.json) accepts the NaN literal; every comparison with NaN is False, so the sender's balance becomes NaN and subsequent transfers and withdrawals are unlimited. Recipients are credited with no matching debit.
finding.source: JSON body field 'amount' set to NaN, attacker-controlled (line 10 on /transfer, line 20 on /withdraw).
finding.sink: BAL[g.user] -= amount (line 13 and line 23) and BAL[to] += amount (line 14)

trace.note: amount=NaN parsed by request.json
BAL < NaN is False, check passes
sender balance becomes NaN
on /withdraw, amount<=0 and BAL<amount are both False with NaN, check passes
recipient credited with no matching debit; transferring NaN also corrupts the victim balance

finding.guards_checked: Balance checks at lines 11 and 21 exist but are defeated by NaN. No finiteness validation on amount. amount<=0 at line 21 is also False for NaN. Severity HIGH: cross-user value creation from an authenticated position; same identity dependency as BIZ-1.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only controls are the balance checks at bank.py:11 (`BAL[g.user] < amount`) and bank.py:21 (`amount <= 0 or BAL[g.user] < amount`). Both are comparisons that evaluate to False when amount is NaN, so they pass. There is no isfinite or type validation on amount anywhere in the directory.
verdict.reason: bank.py:10 takes amount straight from request.json, and Python's json accepts NaN; at bank.py:11 and bank.py:21 the NaN comparisons are False so the checks pass, and bank.py:13/23 and bank.py:14 then set the sender's balance to NaN and credit the recipient with no real debit. The attacker only needs whatever authenticated identity populates g.user, which is not set anywhere in this directory (no auth middleware in bank.py), so the auth assumption is unverified, but the NaN bypass itself does not depend on the role.

finding.claim: Check-then-debit is not atomic. The balance read at line 11 (line 21 on /withdraw) and the debit at line 13 (line 23) have no lock, transaction, compare-and-swap or idempotency key, so concurrent requests can overdraw an account and, on transfer, credit recipients more than the sender lost.
finding.source: Concurrent authenticated requests on the same account, attacker-controlled timing.

trace.note: balance check passes for both concurrent requests when balance covers one amount
both requests debit; sender goes negative
both requests credit recipients; total credited exceeds total debited

finding.guards_checked: No lock, DB transaction, compare-and-swap or idempotency key on /transfer or /withdraw. Triage: window is microseconds in a single process, but no serialization closes it under threaded concurrency. Validation tier 1 (needs concurrent clients in staging). Severity HIGH: financial loss, not self-affecting because recipients gain value.

verdict.guard_found: none. bank.py has no lock, transaction, compare-and-swap or idempotency check. The only controls are the balance comparisons at bank.py:11 and bank.py:21, and they are the check half of the check-then-debit race, not a guard against concurrency. The abort(400) calls at bank.py:12 and bank.py:22 fire only before the debit and do not serialize concurrent requests.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: the balance check at bank.py:11 is followed by the unguarded debit at bank.py:13 and credit at bank.py:14, and /withdraw has the same pattern at bank.py:21 and bank.py:23. Any authenticated user who can reach these routes can send concurrent requests, and no control in the file blocks the overdraw. The one unverified assumption is that g.user is set by authentication middleware outside this file, which I could not inspect, but it does not change the verdict.

finding.claim: No rate limiting on /transfer or /withdraw. Nothing bounds how many money-moving requests an account can send, which makes BIZ-3 easier to trigger and lets an attacker automate BIZ-1 and BIZ-2 at volume.
finding.source: Any request to /transfer (line 7) or /withdraw (line 18), repeated at will.
finding.sink: Balance mutations at lines 13-14 and 23 (protected operations lacking throttle)

/withdraw declared with no limiter decorator

finding.guards_checked: No limiter decorator or middleware in bank.py. Rate limiting may exist at the gateway; no such config is in the tree. Severity MEDIUM (abuse risk on payment endpoints).

verdict.guard_found: none: bank.py:7 and bank.py:18 are bare @app.route decorators with no limiter, and the only rate-limit hits in the tree are docs in .claude/skills/security-research/ (no limiter config or middleware in code); gateway-level limiting is unverifiable from this tree.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (bank.py:7 and bank.py:18 declare /transfer and /withdraw with no limiter), and the attacker only needs to reach these endpoints as the account holder, so nothing in the code blocks repeated requests; however, the standalone impact is a hardening gap that the triage rules would rate LOW or fold into BIZ-1/BIZ-2/BIZ-3, not MEDIUM.

finding.guards_checked: No existence check on 'to' before mutation; no transaction or rollback. Self-affecting for the sender (triage Check 10), so LOW. Account-existence oracle is LOW under Check 8.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks are the balance test at bank.py:11, which runs before any mutation, and nothing validates `to` against BAL. There is no try/except, transaction, or rollback around lines 13-14. The `g.user` setter is not in bank.py, so authentication was not verified from this file alone.
verdict.reason: bank.py:9 reads `to` from the JSON body without checking it exists, bank.py:13 debits BAL[g.user] before bank.py:14 raises KeyError for an unknown `to`, and nothing rolls the debit back, so any authenticated user can destroy their own funds and learn account names from the 500-vs-200 response. The effect is self-affecting and low severity, but the trace is accurate and no control blocks it.
